text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu freezes house demolitions in East Jerusalem.
- Netanyahu looking for compromise in conversion law.
- Poll: 40 percent of Israeli youths hate Arabs. 60 percent "want revenge".
JERUSALEM POST
- Court blocks municipal strikes in 14 cities.
- Netanyahu-Mubarak summit to focus on Har Homa.
- Legislators threaten government over Har Homa.
- Sharon: Israel, Jordan to negotiate railway links.
- Tadmor: Koor, Clal can't bid jointly for gas tender.
- Solel Boneh seeks 79 million shekels in share offer.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israeli gesture to Palestinians expected at Israeli-Egyptian summit.
- Senior Palestinian: Negotiations are being held with Jewish settlers concerning compensation for their evacuation.
- Police concerned Russian mafia may try to spring suspect Gregory Lerner from prison.
MAARIV
- Modest expectations ahead of Egyptian-Israeli summit.
- Controversy rages over ultra-orthodox Jews who burned Israeli flag on holiday.
GLOBES
- Industrial production rises by just 0.2 percent in first quarter of 1997.
- No change expected in Israeli interest rates.
